findings.claim: scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binaries uses [ -z "${VAR:-}" ] to gate all four env vars, but this guard does not catch whitespace-only values (e.g. SCP_POLICY_CHECK_OPA_BIN=' '). The whitespace string passes the -z test and is forwarded to scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binary, where it also passes the empty-path guard at line 48 and proceeds to the file-existence check at line 53.
findings.evidence: lib/policy_check_invocation.sh lines 66-74: [ -z "${SCP_POLICY_CHECK_OPA_BIN:-}" ] — POSIX [ -z ] returns false for a single-space string; verify_runtime_binary line 48: [ -z "$path" ] likewise returns false for ' '; the function then reaches [ ! -f ' ' ] at line 53 which is true, emitting SCP-E001 'runtime binary is missing at the configured path' instead of the expected 'empty path or expected SHA256' message. Downstream exit is still non-zero — there is no bypass — but the error code is misleading.
findings.impact: No security bypass: file ' ' does not exist on any plausible system so exit is still non-zero. Operational impact: an operator who accidentally sets an env var to whitespace receives the wrong SCP-E001 message, making the misconfiguration harder to diagnose. The regression test suite does not cover this case.
findings.mitigation: Replace [ -z "${VAR:-}" ] with a compound guard: [ -z "${VAR:-}" ] || [[ "${VAR}" =~ ^[[:space:]]+$ ]], or use parameter expansion to strip whitespace before the check. Alternatively add a test_wrapper_rejects_whitespace_only_opa_bin test case to pin the diagnostic output.

findings.claim: scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binary does not validate that the label parameter is non-empty. An empty label produces a printf output of ' runtime binary verification refused:...' (leading space after the format delimiter) that may confuse log parsers.
findings.evidence: lib/policy_check_invocation.sh line 49: printf '%s %s: %s\n' "$code" "$file" "$message" in scp_policy_check_emit_error expands label via the message string — no guard. No current caller passes an empty label, but the precondition is undocumented.
findings.impact: Cosmetic only. No correctness or security impact under any observed call path.
findings.mitigation: Document the label parameter as required-non-empty in a brief inline comment, or add a one-line assertion: [ -n "$label" ] || { ...; return 1; }.

findings.claim: test_inner_function_rejects_path_set_expected_empty and test_inner_function_rejects_path_empty_expected_set assert only returncode != 0 and do not inspect stderr content, providing weaker regression coverage on the diagnostic output compared to test_inner_function_rejects_both_empty.
findings.evidence: tests/scripts/test_empty_sha_bypass.py lines 48-55: both single-input-empty tests check only res.returncode != 0; contrast with lines 42-45 which additionally assert 'empty path' in res.stderr.lower() or 'refused' in res.stderr.lower(). If the error message is silently dropped the two weaker tests still pass.
findings.impact: Reduced fidelity in detecting future regressions to diagnostic output. No correctness impact today.
findings.mitigation: Add stderr assertions to both tests mirroring the pattern in test_inner_function_rejects_both_empty.

structured_review.summary: fr3 correctly closes R3-SAF-MAJ-01. scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binary now refuses empty path or empty expected SHA at lib/policy_check_invocation.sh lines 48-51 before any file I/O or SHA computation; scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binaries performs an explicit pre-flight emptiness sweep across all four required env vars (lines 66-74) and emits a single aggregated error naming all missing vars before delegating. All seven cases in tests/scripts/test_empty_sha_bypass.py — both-empty, path-empty-only, expected-empty-only, all-unset, and each of the four single-var-unset partial scenarios — map correctly to the new guards and the error message strings match. One MIN finding (whitespace-only env var value not caught by -z guard but caught downstream by file-existence check — not a bypass, only a misleading diagnostic) and two nit findings (undocumented label precondition; partial stderr coverage in two inner-function tests). No CRIT or MAJ findings. §4.3 fixpoint condition is satisfied: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (MIN/nit only).
